{
  "screen_decision": "include",
  "screen_rationale": "The study quantifies the concordance between mouse models and human inflammatory diseases by analyzing gene expression patterns and reporting correlation coefficients (Spearman's rank correlation coefficient: 0.43–0.68) and percentages of genes changed in the same direction (77–93%). This directly measures the agreement between animal model results and human clinical outcomes.",
  "arm": "disease-biology",
  "arm_evidence": "Here we reevaluated the same gene expression datasets used in the previous study by focusing on genes whose expression levels were significantly changed in both humans and mice. Contrary to the previous findings, the gene expression levels in the mouse models showed extraordinarily significant correlations with those of the human conditions",
  "therapeutic_areas": [
    "sepsis-inflammation",
    "infectious-disease"
  ],
  "areas_evidence": "Genomic responses in mouse models greatly mimic human inflammatory diseases. transcriptome analysis | inflammation | sepsis | burn | trauma",
  "model_type": "across-multiple-models",
  "model_evidence": "The study analyzes multiple mouse models for different conditions (burn, trauma, sepsis, infection) and compares them to human data for the same conditions.",
  "species": [
    "mouse"
  ],
  "species_evidence": "Genomic responses in mouse models greatly mimic human inflammatory diseases.",
  "endpoint_class": "secondary-biomarker",
  "endpoint_evidence": "The study focuses on gene expression levels and transcriptome analysis, which are biomarkers, rather than hard clinical outcomes like mortality or survival."
}
